class.name: PorchlightProgress
class.brief_description: Stores and recoverably persists completed Porchlight milestones.
class.description: The global Porchlight milestone-state service. Completed milestones are stored persistently in completion order and automatically loaded when the singleton is created. Milestone names are normalized by removing leading and trailing whitespace. Use [method complete_milestone] and [method remove_milestone] for individual changes. Use [method complete_milestones] and [method remove_milestones] to apply an ordered batch with one save operation. The default save path is [code]user://porchlight_progress.cfg[/code]. Use [method set_save_path] to switch transactionally to another file below [code]user://[/code], such as a profile or save-slot file. Changing the save path loads and validates the target before changing either the active path or milestone state. A missing target file represents valid empty progress unless a valid backup is available for recovery. A failed path change preserves the previous path and state. Newly written progress files use save-format version [code]1[/code]. Existing unversioned files are treated as legacy version [code]0[/code] and remain loadable. A legacy file is upgraded to the current format the next time it is saved. Malformed version metadata is rejected with [constant ERR_INVALID_DATA]. Files using a newer unsupported version are rejected with [constant ERR_FILE_UNRECOGNIZED]. Saves are written to a validated temporary file before the primary file is replaced. When the current primary file is valid, it is preserved as a last-known-good [code].bak[/code] file before promotion. The first save for a new slot does not create a backup because no prior primary exists. A missing or damaged primary file is automatically restored from a valid backup during loading. A primary file using an unsupported future save format is never replaced by its backup. Abandoned [code].tmp[/code] files are ignored during loading and removed before the next save attempt. Calling [method load_progress] at runtime replaces the active state from the current save file and emits [signal progress_reloaded] when milestone membership changes. The singleton's initial constructor load is silent. Automatic saves performed by milestone mutations always use the current path returned by [method get_save_path].

method.name: clear_milestones
method.description: Removes every completed milestone and recoverably saves the empty progress state to the active save path using the current save format. Emits [signal milestones_cleared] if at least one milestone was completed before the operation.

method.name: complete_milestone
method.description: Marks [param milestone] as complete and recoverably saves the updated progress to the active save path. Returns [code]true[/code] if the milestone was newly completed. Returns [code]false[/code] if its normalized name is empty or it was already complete. A newly completed milestone is appended to the ordered list returned by [method get_completed_milestones] and causes [signal milestone_completed] to be emitted.

method.name: complete_milestones
method.description: Marks every normalized entry in [param milestones] as complete. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed, empty entries are ignored, and duplicate names are discarded while preserving their first occurrence. Returns the milestones that became newly complete, in normalized input order. Milestones that were already complete are omitted from the returned array. The full batch is applied before signals are emitted. Progress is recoverably saved once to the active save path when at least one milestone changes, then [signal milestone_completed] is emitted once for each returned milestone in order. Returns an empty array without saving or emitting signals when no milestone changes.

method.name: get_completed_count
method.description: Returns the number of currently completed milestones.

method.name: get_completed_milestones
method.description: Returns the completed milestones as an [Array] of [StringName] values. The milestones are returned in the order they were completed or loaded from the active save file.

method.name: get_save_path
method.description: Returns the currently active progress save path. The initial path is [code]user://porchlight_progress.cfg[/code]. A successful call to [method set_save_path] replaces it. The corresponding recovery backup path is the active path followed by [code].bak[/code].

method.name: is_complete
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param milestone] is currently complete. Returns [code]false[/code] when the normalized milestone name is empty.

method.name: load_progress
method.description: Reloads completed milestones from the active save path. Returns [constant OK] when loading succeeds. If the primary file is missing and a valid [code].bak[/code] file exists, the backup is restored to the primary path and loaded. If neither a primary nor a valid backup exists, the slot is treated as empty progress and returns [constant OK]. If the primary file is malformed or otherwise unreadable and a valid backup exists, the backup is restored and loaded. If both the primary and backup are invalid, the primary load error is returned. An unsupported future-version primary returns [constant ERR_FILE_UNRECOGNIZED] and is not replaced by an older backup. Unversioned files are interpreted as legacy save-format version [code]0[/code]. Files explicitly declaring the current version [code]1[/code] are loaded normally. A non-integer or negative format version returns [constant ERR_INVALID_DATA]. A format version newer than the engine supports returns [constant ERR_FILE_UNRECOGNIZED]. Empty entries, unsupported entry types, and duplicate milestone names inside an otherwise valid milestone array are ignored. Abandoned [code].tmp[/code] files are not considered loading candidates. If the loaded membership differs from the active state, the full replacement is applied before [signal progress_reloaded] is emitted. Added milestones are reported in loaded-file order, and removed milestones are reported in previous completion order. A reload that only changes milestone ordering installs the loaded order without emitting [signal progress_reloaded]. If loading, backup restoration, or validation fails, the active milestone state and save path are preserved and no reload signal is emitted.

method.name: remove_milestone
method.description: Removes [param milestone] from completed progress and recoverably saves the updated state to the active save path. Returns [code]true[/code] if the milestone was removed. Returns [code]false[/code] if its normalized name is empty or it was not complete. A successful removal emits [signal milestone_removed].

method.name: remove_milestones
method.description: Removes every normalized entry in [param milestones] from completed progress. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed, empty entries are ignored, and duplicate names are discarded while preserving their first occurrence. Returns the milestones that were actually removed, in normalized input order. Milestones that were not complete are omitted from the returned array. The full batch is applied before signals are emitted. Progress is recoverably saved once to the active save path when at least one milestone changes, then [signal milestone_removed] is emitted once for each returned milestone in order. Returns an empty array without saving or emitting signals when no milestone changes.

method.name: save_progress
method.description: Recoverably writes the current ordered milestone list to the active save path. The new state is first written to a [code].tmp[/code] file and read back through the normal save-format validator. An abandoned temporary file from an earlier interrupted attempt is removed before this write. If the existing primary is valid, it is copied and validated as the last-known-good [code].bak[/code] file before the temporary state is promoted. The backup therefore contains the state that preceded the current successful save. An invalid existing primary does not replace an already valid backup. A primary declaring an unsupported future format causes the save to return [constant ERR_FILE_UNRECOGNIZED] without replacing the primary. If promotion fails and a valid backup exists, Porchlight attempts to restore the backup to the primary path. New saves include [code]format_version=1[/code]. Saving a loaded legacy unversioned file upgrades that file to version [code]1[/code]. Missing parent directories below [code]user://[/code] are created recursively. Returns the resulting [enum Error] value from writing, validation, backup creation, promotion, or restoration.

method.name: set_save_path
method.description: Transactionally switches progress persistence to [param save_path]. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed and backslashes are converted to forward slashes. The normalized path must identify a file below [code]user://[/code]. Empty paths, directories, other schemes, invalid filename components, and [code].[/code] or [code]..[/code] traversal components return [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER]. The target file, including its format version and any required backup recovery, is completely loaded and validated before the active path or milestone state changes. If the target primary is missing or damaged and a valid [code].bak[/code] file exists, the backup is restored and loaded. A missing target without a valid backup is accepted as an empty save slot. Unversioned targets are accepted as legacy version [code]0[/code]. Invalid version metadata returns [constant ERR_INVALID_DATA], while unsupported future versions return [constant ERR_FILE_UNRECOGNIZED]. A future-version primary is not replaced by a supported backup. If loading or recovery fails, the previous path and milestone state are preserved and no path or reload signal is emitted. After a successful switch, the new path and complete loaded state are installed before any signal is emitted. If membership changed, [signal progress_reloaded] is emitted first. [signal save_path_changed] is then emitted for every successful path change. Assigning the already active normalized path returns [constant OK] without reloading, saving, recovering, or emitting signals.

signal.name: milestone_completed
signal.description: Emitted when [param milestone] becomes complete. Batch completion emits this signal once per changed milestone, after the entire batch has been applied and its save attempt has completed.

signal.name: milestone_removed
signal.description: Emitted when [param milestone] is removed from completed progress. Batch removal emits this signal once per changed milestone, after the entire batch has been applied and its save attempt has completed.

signal.name: milestones_cleared
signal.description: Emitted when [method clear_milestones] removes one or more completed milestones.

signal.name: progress_reloaded
signal.description: Emitted after [method load_progress] or [method set_save_path] successfully installs a saved or recovered state with different milestone membership. [param added_milestones] contains milestones present in the loaded state but absent from the previous state, in loaded-file order. [param removed_milestones] contains milestones present in the previous state but absent from the loaded state, in previous completion order. The complete loaded state and active save path have already been installed when this signal is emitted. Identical-membership, failed, and initial constructor loads do not emit this signal. During [method set_save_path], this signal is emitted before [signal save_path_changed].

signal.name: save_path_changed
signal.description: Emitted after [method set_save_path] successfully changes the active save path. [param previous_path] is the formerly active normalized path. [param new_path] is the newly active normalized path. The target state, including any recovered backup state, and [param new_path] are fully installed before this signal is emitted. If the switch also changes milestone membership, [signal progress_reloaded] is emitted first. Failed and repeated path assignments do not emit this signal.
